chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Suleiman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about breast-feeding, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'The free woman is not compelled to breast-feed the child, and the mother of the child (slave) is compelled.'

key_terms.أُمُّ الْوَلَدِ: The mother of the child (specifically a slave woman who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in the obligation of breast-feeding between a free woman and a slave woman in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of radāʿ by distinguishing between the legal status of free and enslaved women, establishing that while a free woman is not compelled to breast-feed, an umm al-walad (slave mother) is obligated to do so for her master's benefit. This ruling reflects the socio-legal context of early Shia jurisprudence, where the rights of the master over the slave's labor extended to nursing the child, contrasting with the voluntary nature of the act for free women.
